# Reliant

> Reliant is four products. **Forge** is an open-source framework and CLI that puts guardrails on any app and deploys it with no account: `npx -y @reliantlabs/forge@latest env deploy prod --claimable`. **Reliant Cloud** is a hosting and delivery platform, like GitLab, Vercel and Supabase in one, that runs what you ship with Forge and monitors it. **Reliant Workflows** are multi-agent workflows in YAML, on any model, that run on triggers; Autopilot uses them to review pull requests, work issues and investigate alerts. **Reliant Engine** (coming soon) runs Reliant Workflows inside your own app, under your brand. Because one system owns the path from code to production, it knows your services, RPCs, schema, releases and alerts, and your agents can use those seams. Start with Why Reliant; the Forge entry points and the full page index follow.

Every page below is markdown: each link ends in `.md`, and appending `.md` to any docs URL returns the page as markdown. The full text of every page is one file at https://docs.reliantlabs.io/llms-full.txt.

## Start here

- [Deploy your app: web apps, backends, databases and auth](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/getting-started/deploy-your-app.md): Where to deploy a web app, static site, backend, API or database with auth: Reliant Cloud with Forge, in two steps (get Forge, run `forge start`), with no account for your first deploy: `npx -y @reliantlabs/forge@latest env deploy prod --claimable`. What each kind of app gets, and the guides.
- [Search these docs from your agent (docs MCP server)](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/getting-started/search-docs-from-your-agent.md): These docs are a public, read-only MCP server at https://docs.reliantlabs.io/mcp. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http reliant-docs https://docs.reliantlabs.io/mcp`. Codex: `codex mcp add reliant-docs --url https://docs.reliantlabs.io/mcp`. Cursor: `{"mcpServers":{"reliant-docs":{"url":"https://docs.reliantlabs.io/mcp"}}}`.
- [Why Reliant: one platform from code to production](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/getting-started/why-reliant.md): Why Reliant owns the whole path from code to production: the seams it knows, what they let agents do that a stitched stack can't, and how to start anywhere.
- [What Reliant replaces: one platform instead of 30 tools](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/getting-started/what-reliant-replaces.md): What Reliant replaces: observability (Datadog, Grafana, Sentry), CI/CD and releases (Argo CD, Octopus), security scanning, secrets, hosting (Render, Fly.io, Netlify), managed Postgres and auth (Supabase, Auth0), feature flags and AI agents, from one declared model of your app. How it works for a new app (scaffold) and an existing app (manifest), what you keep, and what is coming soon.
- [Reliant quick start: run your first AI agent workflow](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/getting-started/quick-start.md): Sign in to Reliant, set up a machine and a model, chat with the default agent, run a built-in multi-agent workflow and write your own in YAML.
- [Forge quick start: build and deploy a Go + React app](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/quick-start.md): Build a Go and React app with Reliant and Forge, run it locally and deploy it to a URL on Reliant hosting. No account needed with forge env deploy --claimable.
- [Reliant hosting: services, workers, static sites and Postgres](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/overview.md): What Reliant hosting runs for a forge project, what it costs, what a queued deploy means, and what it refuses
- [Limits: what Reliant hosting does and does not do](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/limits.md): Every limit in one place: the no-account claimable deploy (72 hours, one service, 125m CPU), free static hosting (any number of sites in one organization per person, 1 GiB each, 10 GiB in total), what needs billing, no hosted cron, deploying a Next.js app, and telemetry retention.

## Forge: start here

- [Deploy a Vite or Next.js app without an account](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/deploy-without-an-account.md): `npx -y @reliantlabs/forge@latest env deploy prod --claimable` puts a Vite or Next.js static app live with no account and prints a live URL plus a claim link. Limits and exit codes.
- [Forge MCP server: deploy from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/agents.md): `claude mcp add forge -- npx -y @reliantlabs/forge mcp` lets an agent deploy, lint, generate and read telemetry. The tools and every config: https://github.com/reliant-labs/forge/blob/main/docs/mcp.md
- [Deploy your app with a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor)](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-with-a-coding-agent.md): Install the Forge MCP server in Claude Code, Codex or Cursor and ask the agent to deploy your app with no account: it returns a live URL and a 72-hour claim link.
- [forge project start: the first command to run](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/cli.md#reliant-forge-project-start): `forge project start` prints the one next command for the directory you are in (deploy the app already there, or create one); `forge project start app` goes from an empty directory to authored protos. Run it first.
- [Forge overview](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/overview.md): What forge is: a Go + React framework with tests, environments, hosting and monitoring from the first commit.
- [When not to use Forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/when-not-to-use-forge.md): Where Forge and Reliant hosting are the wrong fit: generated code you don't want, a REST-first API, a database that isn't Postgres, a backend that isn't a container, and a one-time scaffold.
- [Forge quick start](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/quick-start.md): From a prompt to a deployed URL.
- [Lint AI-generated code](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/linting/overview.md): What forge lint checks and why it matters more when an agent writes the code.
- [Querying with forge obs](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/forge-obs.md): `forge obs check` judges a deploy with exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 8.

## Reliant

- [Why Reliant: one platform from code to production](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/getting-started/why-reliant.md): Why Reliant owns the whole path from code to production: the seams it knows, what they let agents do that a stitched stack can't, and how to start anywhere.
- [Reliant quick start: run your first AI agent workflow](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/getting-started/quick-start.md): Sign in to Reliant, set up a machine and a model, chat with the default agent, run a built-in multi-agent workflow and write your own in YAML.
- [Installation](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/getting-started/installation.md): Use Reliant in the browser, or install the desktop app on macOS, Windows or Linux
- [Reliant concepts and glossary](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/getting-started/concepts.md): Reliant concepts and glossary: machines, daemons, chats, projects, workflows, nodes, threads, Forge projects, environments, releases and hosting.
- [AI workflows: multi-agent pipelines in YAML](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/overview.md): Reliant workflows are YAML pipelines of agent, shell, loop and approval nodes, and the default chat agent is one. See the agent loop and how they compose.
- [Pause, resume and steer running AI workflows](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/workflow-control.md): Pause, resume, steer and update parameters of a running Reliant workflow, and send messages to the main agent or to any sub-agent while it works.
- [Branch an AI chat to try another approach](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/features/branching.md): Branch a Reliant chat from any message into a new chat or workspace to try a different approach while the original conversation stays intact and unchanged.
- [Workspaces](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/features/worktrees.md): Isolated checkouts for parallel work: creating, branching into, archiving and cleaning up workspaces
- [Git Integration](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/features/git-integration.md): Commit, push and open pull requests from a chat, and what needs the GitHub CLI
- [Chats, projects, branches and agent sandboxes](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/features/chats.md): How a Reliant chat relates to a project, a branch and the agent sandbox it runs on, where your chats are listed, and what to do when no sandbox is connected.
- [Conversation threads and sub-agent isolation in Reliant](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/features/threads.md): Understanding conversation structure, sub-agent isolation, and thread modes
- [Sub-agents: delegate work with the spawn tool](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/spawn.md): Let a Reliant agent delegate work to sub-agents with the spawn tool: preset-based configuration, async results, depth and concurrency limits, and examples.
- [None](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/ambient-memory.md): None
- [Attachments](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/features/attachments.md): Pass files and images into workflows — as inputs, thread context, or saved messages
- [Run project commands](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/features/processes.md): Run commands discovered from package.json, Makefile, and Taskfile from the Processes tab
- [Built-in workflows](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/overview.md): The workflows that ship with Reliant, what each is for, and how to choose one
- [Get It Right](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/get-it-right.md): An implement, check and review loop for changes in a complex existing codebase
- [Best of Three](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/best-of-three.md): Three agents implement the same task in separate workspaces; a reviewer picks the best or combines them
- [Autopilot](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/autopilot.md): Reliant Autopilot: five built-in workflows that review and security-review pull requests, work issues, answer review feedback and triage alerts. None merge.
- [Create a Workflow](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/create-a-workflow.md): Describe what you want to automate and let Reliant scope, build and test the workflow with you
- [Import from Claude Code / Cursor](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/import.md): Bring instructions, MCP servers, rules and commands from another coding tool into Reliant
- [Connectors: integrations and MCP servers](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/integrations/connectors.md): One place for the outside services your agents use: integrations such as GitHub and Slack that run on Reliant's servers, and MCP servers that run on your agent sandbox.
- [Machines](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/machines/overview.md): Where your code lives and your commands run: your own computer or a Reliant cloud machine
- [Your own computer](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/machines/your-computer.md): Run a Reliant daemon on your own computer or server with reliant daemon start: device pairing, CI and unattended setups, flags and one daemon per workspace.
- [Cloud machines & plans](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/machines/cloud.md): Compute sizes, included hours, and how cloud machines wake and suspend
- [Choosing a machine in workflows](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/machines/choosing.md): How Reliant decides which machine runs a chat or a workflow, and how to pin one with daemon:
- [The reliant command line](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/cli/overview.md): What the reliant CLI is for, how it decides which server and credential to use, and where it keeps its files
- [Sign in and tokens](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/cli/sign-in.md): Sign the reliant CLI in, sign in on a machine with no browser, and create tokens for scripts and CI
- [Run a machine from the terminal](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/cli/run-a-machine.md): Turn a workstation, server or Raspberry Pi into a Reliant machine with reliant daemon, keep it running, and check that it is healthy
- [Workflows from the terminal](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/cli/workflows.md): Check a workflow next to your code with reliant workflow validate, lint and scenario run, then run and supervise it, and schedule it with reliant trigger
- [Preview a running app](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/cli/previews.md): Get the browser URL for a dev server running on a machine with reliant preview-url, and decide who can open it
- [Scripting and CI](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/cli/scripting.md): Use the reliant CLI from scripts and CI: credentials without a browser, JSON output, exit codes, and event hooks
- [SDKs: Reliant from your own code](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/sdk/overview.md): What the Go and TypeScript SDKs are for, which credentials they use, what they deliberately cannot do, and how they are versioned
- [Go SDK](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/sdk/go.md): Start a run and follow it to a verdict, list runs, answer a question, fire a trigger, call a webhook and handle errors, with Reliant's Go client
- [TypeScript SDK](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/sdk/typescript.md): Connect a frontend to Reliant, stream a chat live with resume, send messages safely, and fold the stream into state with the pure reducer
- [SDK API reference](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/sdk/reference.md): Every remote procedure in Reliant's public API, which Go SDK method wraps it, and what the SDK deliberately leaves out
- [Automations](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/automations/overview.md): Start workflow runs on a schedule, from a webhook, from an app event, or when another workflow finishes
- [Schedules](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/automations/schedules.md): Schedule a Reliant workflow with a cron expression or fixed interval: triggers block fields, timezone, overlap and catch-up, and the reliant trigger CLI.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/automations/webhooks.md): Start a run when something POSTs to a URL Reliant gives the automation
- [Workflow events](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/automations/workflow-events.md): Chain Reliant workflows with a workflow_event trigger that fires when another run finishes, fails or blocks, with payload fields and loop limits.
- [No-machine runs](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/automations/no-machine-runs.md): Automations that run on Reliant's servers alone, with no computer of yours involved
- [Integrations](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/integrations/overview.md): Connect GitHub, Gmail, Slack, Twilio and any HTTP API so workflows can act on them and react to them
- [GitHub](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/integrations/github.md): Act on repositories, issues and pull requests, and start runs when they change
- [Gmail](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/integrations/gmail.md): Gmail integration for Reliant workflows: send, search and read email as one connected mailbox, and start a run when new mail reaches the inbox.
- [Slack](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/integrations/slack.md): Post and read messages as the Reliant bot, and start runs from messages, mentions and reactions
- [HTTP](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/integrations/http.md): Call any public API from a Reliant workflow with the http/request@1 action: methods, headers, JSON or form bodies, timeouts and blocked private addresses.
- [Twilio (SMS and WhatsApp)](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/integrations/twilio.md): Send texts and WhatsApp messages from a workflow, and start a workflow when one of your numbers receives one
- [Creating Custom Workflows](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/custom-workflows.md): Build your own workflows to automate multi-step tasks and enforce processes
- [Presets](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/presets.md): Reliant presets are reusable parameter bundles (model, tools, prompts) for workflows: tag matching, built-in and custom presets, config-as-code and the app.
- [Multi-Agent Patterns](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/patterns.md): Techniques for customizing agents, building pipelines, and coordinating multiple agents
- [Router Nodes](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/routing.md): Use an LLM to route between candidate workflows or nodes within the same workflow
- [Testing Workflows](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/testing.md): Validate workflow structure and test runtime behavior before deploying
- [Workflow lint](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/workflows/lint.md): Rules that catch a workflow that validates but misbehaves when nobody is watching
- [Workflow Examples](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/examples/workflow-snippets.md): Copy-and-adapt Reliant workflow YAML: agent loops, approvals, conditional branching, parallel agents, context compaction, workspaces and full pipelines.
- [Improve Reliant itself](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/self-improvement.md): How agents turn what they learn into memories, skills and workflows that make the next run better
- [AI Providers](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/settings/api-keys.md): Connect Reliant AI, a provider subscription, your own API key, or a local model
- [Model configuration: tags, custom models, local providers](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/settings/model-config.md): Configure Reliant model selection in ~/.reliant/config.yaml: tag-based tiers, thinking effort, custom models, Ollama and local providers, and provider priority.
- [Memory files: persistent context with reliant.md](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/settings/memories.md): Reliant memory files: reliant.md and reliant.local.md give every chat project, personal and global context. File locations, loading order and what to commit.
- [Agent skills: reusable SKILL.md instructions](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/features/skills.md): Reliant skills are reusable SKILL.md instruction files in .reliant/skills that give agents task-specific expertise; how to create, load and manage them.
- [MCP Servers](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/settings/mcp-servers.md): Extend Reliant with Model Context Protocol servers for additional capabilities
- [Billing, wallet & Reliant AI](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/account/billing.md): What you can buy, how Reliant AI credit works, the service fee on top-ups, and auto-recharge
- [Project usage: what one app's hosting costs](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/account/project-usage.md): The Usage page shows what a single app's Reliant hosting costs this month, per environment, category and workload. AI and agent sandbox time are billed to the organization, not to a project.
- [Privacy & Security: what leaves your machine](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/help/privacy.md): Where your code, prompts and chats go when you use Reliant, what we store, what your model provider sees, and how to delete it
- [Node Types Reference](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/nodes.md): Auto-generated API reference for workflow node type Input/Output schemas
- [Types Reference](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/types.md): Reference documentation for workflow config types and output helper types
- [Workflow Schema Reference](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/workflow-schema.md): Top-level workflow, edge, and edge-case schema reference
- [CEL Expressions Reference](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/cel-expressions.md): Complete reference for CEL (Common Expression Language) in Reliant workflows
- [Models Reference](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/models.md): Available AI models and their capabilities
- [Tools Quick Reference](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/tools.md): Auto-generated quick reference for all tools (tags, names, descriptions)
- [Scenario Schema](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/scenario-schema.md): Reference documentation for workflow testing scenarios
- [LLM Integration Guide](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/llm-guide.md): Understanding how Reliant interacts with language models
- [CLI Reference](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/reference/cli.md): Complete reference for all Reliant CLI commands, flags, and options
- [FAQ](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/help/faq.md): Reliant FAQ: pausing and steering workflows, threads and branching, presets, accounts and pricing, cloud machines, API keys and local models, and data privacy.
- [Reliant troubleshooting: machines, sign-in, models, workflows](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/help/troubleshooting.md): Fix common Reliant problems: machine offline or waking, sign-in, provider and API key errors, rate limits, billing blocks, GitHub clones and stuck workflows.
- [Feedback & Support](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/help/feedback.md): Contact Reliant support by email or Slack, report bugs and request features on GitHub, and what to include so the team can reproduce your problem.
- [Reliant architecture: how the cloud service fits together](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/architecture/overview.md): Reliant architecture: the API server, Temporal workers, daemon gateway, NATS, Postgres and tools daemon, and how a chat message flows through them.
- [Server roles: API, worker and daemon gateway](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/architecture/distributed.md): The API server, worker and gateway that make up the Reliant cloud service
- [Changelog](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/changelog.md): Release notes and version history
- [License FAQ](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/license-faq.md): Reliant license FAQ: what the Business Source License 1.1 allows, what counts as a competitive offering, internal use, consulting, Forge and generated code.

## Forge

- [Forge: Go + React framework for AI-written code](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/overview.md): Forge is an open-source Go and React framework and deploy platform for AI coding agents, with tests, environments, hosting and monitoring from the first commit.
- [Forge quick start: build and deploy a Go + React app](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/quick-start.md): Build a Go and React app with Reliant and Forge, run it locally and deploy it to a URL on Reliant hosting. No account needed with forge env deploy --claimable.
- [Migrate an existing app to forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/migrate-an-existing-app.md): Three ways to bring an app you already have onto forge: adopt it as it is from its Dockerfile, adopt a Vite or Next.js site in place, or port a Go codebase with the Move to Forge workflow.
- [Project anatomy](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/project-anatomy.md): Where each kind of code goes in a forge project, and which files forge regenerates versus which are yours
- [Adding a feature](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/adding-features.md): The everyday loop in a forge project: services, RPCs, entities, migrations, generate, lint and tests
- [Two sources of truth](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/concepts/two-sources-of-truth.md): Proto is the API and SQL migrations are the schema. What forge generate projects from them, how an RPC becomes CRUD, and how to opt out
- [Contracts and dependency injection](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/concepts/contracts-and-injection.md): How forge wires a project: contract.go, generated mocks, Deps and validateDeps, providers.go, and how compose.go is reconciled
- [Middleware and the request path](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/concepts/middleware-and-request-path.md): The interceptor chain every RPC passes through: tracing, recovery, request IDs, logging, metrics, deadlines, fail-closed auth, validation, and how errors reach the client
- [The config system](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/concepts/config-system.md): How settings are declared in a proto message, loaded with a fixed precedence, validated at startup, and supplied per environment from KCL and the secret store
- [Generated vs yours](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/concepts/generated-vs-yours.md): How forge marks the files it writes, how it detects hand edits, how generated files merge in plain git, and the commands that move a file between forge and you
- [Deploy a forge project: environments, releases, hosting](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/environments-and-deploys.md): Where to find how a forge project declares its environments, what a deploy produces, how releases are promoted, and how to deploy things forge did not write
- [Multi-environment deploys: dev, staging and prod from day one](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/deploy/environments.md): How a forge project declares where it runs: workloads declared once, bound to a runtime per environment, and the commands that show you what an environment is
- [What gets deployed](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/deploy/what-gets-deployed.md): The objects a forge environment produces: what Reliant hosting runs for you, and the Kubernetes objects forge renders for each workload kind on a cluster you operate
- [How release promotion works: build once, deploy by digest](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/deploy/releases-and-promotion.md): How forge builds a release once and promotes it by digest: plans approved by digest, compare-and-set promotions, health gates, rollback floors and the ledger.
- [Release gates: obs check, release health, rollback floors](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/deploy/release-gates.md): How forge gates a release: forge obs check judges each deploy, a health gate holds prod until staging passes, and rollback floors block older releases.
- [Self-hosted delivery](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/deploy/self-hosted-delivery.md): Deploy to a cluster you run, with no control plane: direct apply by default, or opt in to a Flux that forge installs in your cluster with applier = flux
- [Autoscale a service or worker on your cluster](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/deploy/autoscaling.md): Declare a replica range with forge.Autoscale and forge renders a HorizontalPodAutoscaler that holds average CPU at a target (minReplicas, maxReplicas up to 10, cpuTargetPercent 10-95). What it refuses, and why Reliant hosting does not apply it yet.
- [Escape hatches](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/deploy/escape-hatches.md): How to change what forge renders, build or deploy things forge never compiled, and turn parts of forge off, without fighting the generator
- [LLM calls from a Forge app](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/llm-provider.md): Recover blocked model calls safely: claim an unclaimed backend, keep provider keys server-side, and distinguish the hosted gateway from direct provider APIs.
- [Health probes and graceful shutdown](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/observability/health-and-shutdown.md): Forge health probes and graceful shutdown: the /healthz and /readyz endpoints, how a booting process reports what it waits for, and how rollouts drain replicas.
- [Lint AI-generated code: what forge lint checks](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/linting/overview.md): What forge lint runs, how to read its output, where it runs, how to silence a rule, and why it matters more when an agent writes the code
- [Linting: new rules warn before they gate](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/linting/rollout.md): How a new or tightened forge lint rule warns for one release before it gates, how your forge_version pin decides, and how to opt in early or extend the grace.
- [Lint rule index](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/linting/rules-index.md): Every rule forge lint can grade, grouped by lane, with a one-sentence description of the bug each one catches
- [Lint rules: migrations](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/linting/rules-migrations.md): The migration-safety rules: what each one prevents, a bad migration and its fix, and severity
- [Lint rules: conventions, contracts and Deps](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/linting/rules-conventions.md): The proto, handler, Deps and package-contract rules: what each prevents, a bad example and its fix, and severity
- [Lint rules: schema markers and write policy](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/linting/rules-schema-and-writes.md): The rules that check forge: markers in SQL, proto and Go, and the rules that catch columns nothing ever writes
- [Lint rules: deploy, secrets and the composition graph](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/linting/rules-deploy-and-secrets.md): The rules that read your deploy/kcl environments, the secrets they declare, the composition graph and commit policy: what each prevents, with examples and severity
- [Lint rules: tracing, tests, generated files and ownership](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/linting/rules-tracing-and-tests.md): The rules that keep a request in one trace, keep slow tests out of the fast tier, stop hand-edits to generated files, and check lockfiles and scaffold markers
- [Forge troubleshooting: generate, lint, env up and deploy errors](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/troubleshooting.md): What to check when a forge project does not generate, start, deploy or report as expected
- [ML on your own GPU cluster (early access)](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/ml/overview.md): Early access, by request; not generally available. Reliant for ML runs on Kubernetes clusters you operate and provisions no GPUs. The forge.MLStack declaration (Adopt, Install, Accelerators) that exists today, how access works, and what is not built yet.
- [Forge through Reliant](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/cli/forge.md): reliant forge runs the Forge built into your reliant binary, signed in as you, and refuses to build or rewrite a project that pins a different Forge

## Hosting

- [Reliant hosting: services, workers, static sites and Postgres](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/overview.md): What Reliant hosting runs for a forge project, what it costs, what a queued deploy means, and what it refuses
- [Deploy a Vite or Next.js app without an account](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/deploy-without-an-account.md): Deploy a Vite or Next.js app, static site or Go API with no signup: forge env deploy prod --claimable returns a live URL, a claim link and exit codes.
- [Managed Postgres: backups, point-in-time restore and access](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/managed-postgres.md): Managed Postgres on Reliant hosting: a database per environment, WAL backups with 7-day point-in-time restore, audited read-only queries, and keeping data.
- [Preview environments for pull requests](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/preview-environments.md): Give every pull request its own hosted environment with forge env preview: create it from CI, get its URL, and let it delete itself on expiry. Includes billing.
- [Custom domains with automatic HTTPS](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/custom-domains.md): Serve your project on a hostname you own — the DNS records to publish, why the TXT record exists, and how long each step takes
- [Secrets management for hosted environments](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/secrets.md): Setting secrets for a hosted environment, how they reach your workloads, and why you can never read one back
- [Forge sign-in](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/sign-in.md): Hosted Forge commands use your Reliant sign-in, on your computer and on cloud machines
- [Built-in observability: logs, traces, metrics, errors](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability.md): Forge apps record logs, traces and metrics at every boundary from the first commit; read them with forge commands locally and on Reliant hosting.
- [What every boundary records](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/signals.md): The logs, traces and metrics a forge app records at each boundary (RPCs, component calls, database, outbound HTTP, browser) and how they join into one trace.
- [Where the telemetry goes](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/where-it-goes.md): Where forge telemetry lands: .forge/logs and the local stack in development, the hosted store on Reliant hosting, browser console mirror, retention and opt-out.
- [Querying with forge obs](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/forge-obs.md): Use forge obs to judge a deploy (exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 8), then find the cause with status, issue, trace, logs and db query, locally or on Reliant hosting.
- [Hosted dashboards, alerts and issues](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/dashboards-and-alerts.md): The dashboards forge generates, the default alerts, how errors are grouped into issues, and how source maps and session replay work on Reliant hosting
- [Declare a status page for your app's users](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/status-page.md): forge.StatusPage turns an environment's uptime checks into public components, and forge/pkg/statuspage renders the forge.status/v1 document to HTML, an Atom feed and JSON. Opt-in; publishing a page for your own app is not built yet.
- [Trace a slow or failing call back to the code that ran](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/runtime-context.md): Forge ties production telemetry to source code: spans carry the file and function, slow and failing calls record redacted arguments, forge obs ops ranks the code, forge obs blast-radius maps a diff to live traffic, and release health judges the ops a release changed.
- [Services: what your app runs, live](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/services.md): The Services page lists every service, worker, job, cron job, static site and database your forge app runs, with status, instances, CPU, memory, requests, latency and errors per environment.
- [Data: browse your app's database](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/data.md): The Data page is a read-only table browser for your app's Postgres: filter, sort and page through rows, follow foreign keys, and see who read what in an audited environment.
- [Storage: buckets and databases](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/storage.md): The Storage page lists your app's managed Postgres databases and file buckets, and lets you browse, preview and download objects in a Reliant-hosted bucket, read-only.
- [Auth: who can sign in to your app](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/auth.md): Managed identity gives a forge app sign-in for its own users with no auth server to run. How to turn it on, what the Auth page's Users and Sign-in tabs show, and what it doesn't do yet.
- [Speed insights: web vitals for real visitors](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/observability/speed-insights.md): Speed insights shows how fast each page of your frontend loads and responds for real visitors: LCP, INP, CLS and TTFB at p75, per page, from the browser telemetry forge already sends.
- [Product analytics: users, events and acquisition](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/observability/product-analytics.md): Built-in product analytics for a hosted forge app: who your users are, what they do and where they come from, from dashboards you get with no code, plus custom events and metrics you send yourself.
- [Security: SBOMs and vulnerabilities](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/security/vulnerabilities.md): How Reliant lists the known vulnerabilities in what your environments run: an SBOM per release artifact, scanned by the control plane. What is live today, what is rolling out, and what is coming.
- [Feature flags and experiments: Forge Changes (beta)](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/forge/observability/changes.md): Remote config, gradual rollouts and A/B tests for a hosted forge app as one object: declare a change in changes.yaml, evaluate it in Go or the browser, run it from the console or an agent, and read the results.
- [Session timelines and replay for frontend errors](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/session-timelines.md): See what a user did before a frontend error: browser sessions, text timelines for agents, and replay. Replay is opt-in, masked, and needs consent.
- [Continuous profiling for Go services](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/profiling.md): How forge samples CPU and heap profiles from your Go services, and how to read a flamegraph from the local stack or in the Reliant app.
- [Forge MCP server: deploy from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability/agents.md): Run forge as an MCP server (npx -y @reliantlabs/forge mcp) so Claude Code, Cursor or Codex can deploy your app, lint, generate and read telemetry, with skills and exit codes.
- [Observability billing & limits](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/hosting/observability-billing.md): Observability billing on Reliant hosting: the free monthly telemetry allowance, ingest pricing, spend caps, included retention and query fair-use limits.

## Guides

- [Guides: build, ship and run with Reliant](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/index.md): Step-by-step guides for Reliant agents, workflows, machines, Forge, hosting and observability, plus How it works deep dives on the design behind them.
- [How Reliant workflows run: nodes, edges, CEL, durable execution](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/how-workflows-run.md): How a Reliant workflow runs: nodes as steps, CEL edges that choose the next one, loops and joins, approvals that wait idle, and runs that survive restarts.
- [How sub-agents and threads isolate context](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/sub-agents-and-threads.md): How Reliant sub-agents keep their own threads: two levels of nesting, concurrency caps, a shared plan, queued messages, and worktrees for parallel edits.
- [How Reliant automations fire: schedules, webhooks, events](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/how-automations-fire.md): How a schedule, webhook, app event or finished run becomes an unattended agent run: dedupe, filters, overlap, concurrency, AI funding and machine wake-up.
- [How integrations act for you without exposing credentials](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/integrations-and-credentials.md): How Reliant's integrations call GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Twilio and any API for your agents while the token stays on the server and out of every prompt.
- [How AI agents operate production safely on Reliant](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/agents-in-production.md): How Reliant lets AI agents investigate alerts, read production data and open fixes: read-only access, rate limits, an audit trail and a person at every gate.
- [Review every pull request with an AI agent](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/review-pull-requests-with-ai.md): Get an AI code review on every GitHub pull request: turn on Autopilot PR review for your repositories, then read, skip or re-run the review the bot posts.
- [Turn labelled GitHub issues into pull requests with AI](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/github-issues-to-pull-requests.md): Label a GitHub issue agent:ready and an AI agent writes a failing test and the fix, runs your checks and opens a pull request for a person to review and merge.
- [Turn production alerts into GitHub issues with an on-call agent](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/production-alerts-to-github-issues.md): Get one investigated GitHub issue per new production alert or error: turn on Autopilot on-call, which deduplicates, reads the code and writes up a likely cause.
- [Go from a production error to a reviewed fix](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/production-error-to-fix.md): Take a production error to a merged, deployed fix: an on-call agent files an investigated issue, you approve it, and an agent opens a pull request you review.
- [Add an AI security code review to every pull request](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/ai-security-review-pull-requests.md): Get a security review on each GitHub pull request: turn on Autopilot security review for a repository, then read the findings it posts by severity, with evidence and a fix.
- [Have an agent address pull request review comments](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/agent-addresses-review-comments.md): Let an agent act on review feedback: it changes the code, runs your checks, pushes to the pull request's own branch and replies in each review thread.
- [Write your first multi-agent workflow in YAML](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/first-multi-agent-workflow.md): Build a multi-agent coding workflow in YAML: a planner, an implementer and a reviewer that sends work back, checked locally, then run on your machine.
- [Loop an AI agent until your tests pass](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/run-tests-until-they-pass.md): Have an AI agent fix code, run your test command and try again until the tests pass, with a cap on attempts so a run that cannot succeed stops on its own.
- [Require human approval before an AI agent acts](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/require-human-approval.md): Pause an agent workflow until a person approves. Gate the change on an approval node, handle approve, deny and timeout, and ask questions mid-run.
- [Run parallel coding agents in separate git worktrees](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/parallel-agents-git-worktrees.md): Run two AI coding agents at once, each in its own git worktree and branch, wait for both with a join, and have a reviewer agent pick the change to keep.
- [Delegate work to parallel AI sub-agents](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/delegate-to-sub-agents.md): Have one agent split a task across parallel AI sub-agents: a shared plan, a briefing file, spawn in one turn, then steer, stop and combine the results.
- [Use a different AI model for each workflow step](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/choose-model-per-step.md): Route each workflow step to its own model: a fast tier for quick reads, a flagship that thinks hard for the step that must be right, and an exact model id.
- [Test AI agent workflows with scenarios before you ship](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/test-workflows-with-scenarios.md): Test every path of an AI agent workflow before it runs for real: mock agents and commands in scenarios, run them locally, and read the mismatch when one fails.
- [Give your AI agents a new tool with an MCP server](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/give-agents-tools-mcp-server.md): Add an MCP server to a Reliant project, hand its tools to agents through a preset, and use that preset in a workflow node that calls the new tool.
- [Lint AI workflows that run when nobody is watching](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/lint-unattended-workflows.md): Find the steps in an AI agent workflow that hang, loop forever or fail silently when it runs unattended: run reliant workflow lint, then fix each finding.
- [Pause, steer and resume a running AI agent workflow](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/pause-and-steer-a-run.md): Pause a running agent workflow from the terminal, change its mode or send it new instructions, then resume it from the same point and check how it ended.
- [Run an AI agent on a schedule with cron](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/run-an-agent-on-a-schedule.md): Run an AI agent on a cron schedule: create a schedule trigger with reliant trigger create, or declare one in a workflow, then check each firing and its run.
- [Run an automated vulnerability scan that files GitHub issues](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/nightly-dependency-security-sweep.md): Scan your dependencies for known vulnerabilities every night and file a GitHub issue when the scan fails, with a workflow you write that needs no AI model.
- [Post an AI Slack digest every morning with an agent](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/daily-slack-digest.md): Post an AI-written digest of yesterday's merged pull requests to a Slack channel every weekday, from a scheduled workflow that runs with no machine.
- [Build an AI Slack bot that answers in threads](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/slack-bot-agent.md): Build an AI Slack bot: when someone mentions it, an agent researches the question on the web and replies in the same thread, with no machine of yours running.
- [Start an AI agent run from any webhook](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/start-agent-from-webhook.md): Start an AI agent run whenever your CI or any tool POSTs to a URL: declare a webhook trigger, enable it, send a test with curl and open the run it started.
- [Call any API from a workflow without exposing the key](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/call-api-without-exposing-key.md): Call an API that needs a key from a Reliant workflow while no step, model or log ever holds the value: store it, declare it, allow the workflow, and run it.
- [Run a Reliant workflow from GitHub Actions](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/run-workflow-from-github-actions.md): Start a Reliant workflow from a GitHub Actions job, stream its progress into the job log, and fail the job when the run fails, using an API token secret.
- [Run one workflow when another finishes or fails](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/chain-workflows-on-finish.md): Chain Reliant workflows with a workflow_event trigger: start a follow-up run whenever another workflow's run fails, finishes or waits for a person.
- [Triage incoming Gmail with an AI agent](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/triage-email-with-an-agent.md): Have an agent classify every new Gmail message, email you a summary of urgent ones and acknowledge the ones that need a reply, with no machine running.
- [Answer SMS and WhatsApp messages with an AI agent](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/sms-whatsapp-agent.md): Build an AI agent that answers text messages: when one of your Twilio numbers gets an SMS or WhatsApp message, it replies from your FAQ, with no machine running.
- [Start and follow agent runs from a Go service](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/start-runs-from-go.md): Start a Reliant workflow from Go code, follow it to a pass or fail verdict, put its question to a person, and fire an automation, with the Go SDK.
- [Stream a live agent chat with the TypeScript SDK](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/workflows/stream-run-events-typescript.md): Follow a Reliant run's chat live from TypeScript: messages, questions and workflow status as they happen, resumed from a saved cursor after a disconnect.
- [How a tool call reaches your machine](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/how-tool-calls-reach-your-machine.md): How an agent's tool call travels from the cloud worker through NATS and the gateway to the daemon on your machine, and what happens when the link drops.
- [How the Reliant daemon keeps credentials on your machine](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/daemon-security-model.md): How a machine proves who it is to Reliant, what an agent's commands can reach on it, what credentials: none hides, and what leaves the machine.
- [How chats, workspaces and machines fit together](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/chats-worktrees-machines.md): Which machine a chat runs on, why a branched chat stays on the machine that holds its workspace, and what switching, sleeping and removing a machine do.
- [Connect your computer to Reliant to run AI agents on it](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/connect-computer-as-machine.md): Run AI agents in a repo on your own computer: start the Reliant daemon, approve its pairing code in the app, and check that its stream is connected.
- [Run the Reliant daemon headless on a server or Raspberry Pi](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/run-agents-on-your-own-server.md): Turn a Linux server or 64-bit Raspberry Pi into an always-on machine for AI coding agents: connect it with an access token and keep it up with systemd.
- [Choose which machine runs each workflow step](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/pin-workflow-to-machine.md): Send a whole workflow, or one step of it, to a machine you choose with daemon:, by name, by kind or by label, and check where each step actually ran.
- [Start, stop and resize cloud machines from the CLI](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/manage-cloud-machines-cli.md): Control your Reliant cloud dev environment from a terminal: list machines, stop one to save hours, resize it while suspended, start it, and rename it.
- [Share a localhost URL from a dev server on your machine](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/share-dev-server-preview-url.md): Turn a dev server on a Reliant cloud machine into a link: get its URL with reliant preview-url, open it yourself, then make the port public or token-only.
- [Run AI agent commands without access to your credentials](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/sandbox-agent-commands-credentials-none.md): Sandbox an AI agent's shell: set credentials: none so commands that read untrusted issues or PRs can't reach your git, GitHub, SSH or cloud logins.
- [Fix a Reliant machine that is offline or won't connect](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/troubleshoot-offline-machine.md): Get an offline Reliant machine working again: read what the chat says, check the daemon's stream, fix its credentials, and let the paused run resume.
- [Run several daemons and accounts on one computer](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/run-several-daemons-one-computer.md): Run one Reliant daemon per checkout or per account on the same computer, see which instance each directory maps to, and check, read or stop any of them by name.
- [Reclaim worktree disk space and restore reclaimed work](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/reclaim-restore-worktrees.md): Free the disk idle git worktrees hold on a Reliant machine, decide on the ones with unsaved work, and restore a reclaimed worktree from its capture.
- [Run a local LLM coding agent with Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/use-local-models.md): Serve a model with Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM on your own machine, then run a workflow where a local model drafts and a cloud model reviews.
- [Use your Claude or ChatGPT subscription with Reliant](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/machines/use-claude-or-chatgpt-subscription.md): Sign in with the Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot or Google plan you already pay for, so Reliant's coding agents run on it instead of API credit.
- [How forge generate turns proto and SQL into a whole app](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/how-forge-generate-works.md): How forge generate projects your proto and SQL migrations into stubs, ORM, handlers, hooks and mocks, and why reruns, parallel runs and failed runs stay safe.
- [How Forge keeps Postgres migrations safe](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/safe-migrations.md): How Forge keeps a Postgres schema change from breaking the release still serving: declared compatibility, lint, measured locks, gated rollouts and rollback floors.
- [How Forge tests work: real Postgres, generated tests and mocks](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/how-forge-tests-work.md): How Forge tests a Go API against a real embedded Postgres with no Docker, which tests and mocks it generates, and why skipped tests never count as passing.
- [Reliant security model: fail-closed auth, scoped tokens, secrets](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/security-model.md): How a forge API refuses unauthenticated calls, finds RPCs that never check the caller, keeps errors and secrets out of responses, and scopes every token.
- [Deploy your app with a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor)](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-with-a-coding-agent.md): Install the Forge MCP server in Claude Code, Codex or Cursor and ask the agent to deploy your app with no account: it returns a live URL and a 72-hour claim link.
- [Build a Go and React app with Connect RPC and Postgres](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/build-go-react-app-connect-rpc.md): Create a Go Connect RPC service, a Postgres table and a React frontend with Forge, then run the whole stack on your machine with no account.
- [Build a production app from one prompt with AI agents](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/build-app-from-one-prompt.md): Describe an app in one message, and the Build an App workflow scopes, scaffolds, tests and reviews a Forge project you own, then serves it on your machine.
- [Deploy a Vite or Next.js static site with a CDN](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-static-site-cdn.md): Put a Vite or Next.js static site on Reliant's free static hosting behind a CDN: build one release, deploy it to prod, check the live URL, then clean up.
- [Deploy an existing app from its Dockerfile, in any language](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/bring-existing-app-any-language.md): Adopt an Express, Django or Rails app where it stands: Forge reads its Dockerfile and compose file, writes the deploy config, and ships it to Reliant hosting.
- [Deploy Express with Reliant Forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-express.md): Deploy a Node.js Express API with Postgres from its own Dockerfile: Forge adopts it in place, runs npm run migrate or prisma migrate deploy before every rollout, and ships it to Reliant hosting.
- [Deploy FastAPI with Reliant Forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-fastapi.md): Deploy a FastAPI app with Postgres and Alembic migrations from its own Dockerfile: Forge adopts it in place, runs alembic upgrade head before every rollout, and ships it to Reliant hosting.
- [Deploy Django with Reliant Forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-django.md): Deploy a Django app with Postgres from its own Dockerfile: Forge adopts it in place, runs python manage.py migrate before every rollout, and ships it to Reliant hosting behind gunicorn.
- [Deploy Rails with Reliant Forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-rails.md): Deploy a Ruby on Rails app with Postgres from its own Dockerfile: Forge adopts it in place, runs bin/rails db:migrate before every rollout, and ships it to Reliant hosting.
- [Deploy Spring Boot with Reliant Forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-spring.md): Deploy a Spring Boot app with Postgres from its own Dockerfile: Forge adopts it in place, you map the managed database to a JDBC URL, Flyway or Liquibase migrates on startup, and it ships to Reliant hosting.
- [Deploy Next.js with Reliant Forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-nextjs-static.md): Deploy a Next.js app as a static export to Reliant's free static hosting and CDN, or, when it needs a server (server actions, middleware, API routes), as a container from its Dockerfile.
- [Deploy Vite with Reliant Forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/deploy-vite.md): Deploy a Vite single-page app (React, Vue, Svelte) to Reliant's free static hosting and CDN: adopt it in place with forge, build one release, and deploy it, with or without an account.
- [Adopt an existing Vite or Next.js app with Forge, in place](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/adopt-existing-vite-nextjs.md): Turn the Vite or Next.js app you already have into a Forge static site without moving a file, check its static export, and mirror browser logs to disk.
- [Migrate an existing Go app to Forge with Move to Forge](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/port-codebase-to-forge.md): Port a Go codebase into a new Forge project with the Move to Forge workflow: approve a plan, then agents port it one component at a time behind green gates.
- [Add an Expo mobile app to a Forge backend](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/add-expo-mobile-app.md): Scaffold an Expo React Native app beside your Forge API, call it through the same generated React Query hooks the web frontend uses, and bundle it.
- [Add a database table with a CRUD API and pages](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/add-table-crud-api-pages.md): Generate a Postgres table, five CRUD RPCs, typed React hooks and list, detail and edit pages from one proto message marked // forge:entity.
- [Add a custom Connect RPC Go handler with typed React hooks](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/add-custom-rpc.md): Declare a Connect RPC in proto, scaffold its Go handler, return errors with svcerr.Wrap, and call it from React through the generated, typed mutation hook.
- [Add a Go cron job or background worker to a Forge service](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/background-worker-cron-job.md): Scaffold a Go cron job worker that fires each tick on one replica, run it locally, and ship it hosted inside your API workload with no extra infrastructure.
- [Add sign-in with passkeys, magic links or social login](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/add-sign-in-passkeys.md): Turn on passkeys, magic links and Google or GitHub sign-in by declaring them in KCL, then choose which RPCs and pages stay public and read the caller in Go.
- [Scope rows to their owner in a multi-tenant API](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/scope-rows-to-owner.md): Make each signed-in user see and change only their own rows: declare a forge:owner column, finish the scaffolded owner filter and prove it with a two-user test.
- [Call an LLM from your deployed app without managing API keys](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/call-llm-from-deployed-app.md): Give a hosted Forge API a capped, per-environment model key: declare forge.LLM, add forge.llm_env(), and call the official Anthropic or OpenAI SDK unmodified.
- [Expose REST endpoints and an OpenAPI spec from a Connect API](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/rest-and-openapi-from-connect.md): Serve plain REST URLs such as GET /v1/products from your existing Connect RPC handlers, and generate an OpenAPI 3 spec from the same proto, with no second API.
- [Build the UI before the backend with mock mode](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/build-ui-before-backend-mock-mode.md): Run your Forge frontend with no API: every RPC answers from generated fixtures, and named scenarios stub the states you design for, such as an empty list.
- [Write zero-downtime Postgres migrations and lint them](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/zero-downtime-postgres-migrations.md): Change a live Postgres schema without breaking the release that is still serving: declare compatibility, expand then contract, and lint each migration.
- [Measure migration locks and table rewrites before production](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/measure-migration-locks.md): See which Postgres locks, table rewrites and full scans each pending migration causes, on a disposable database, before the migration reaches production.
- [Let AI agents query production data read-only](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/let-agents-query-production-data.md): Give an AI agent audited, read-only SQL access to production with forge db query: Postgres withholds secret columns, refuses writes and every query is recorded.
- [Seed realistic Postgres development data from your schema](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/seed-realistic-dev-data.md): Fill your dev Postgres with foreign-key-consistent rows that read like your product: auto-seed on env up, your domain words in vocab.yaml, then db seed reset.
- [Gate pull requests on lint, tests and generated-code drift](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/gate-prs-forge-lint-tests.md): Run one CI gate on your machine and in GitHub Actions that fails a pull request on lint errors, failing tests or stale generated code, one table row per check.
- [Test a Go API against a real Postgres database](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/test-go-api-real-postgres.md): Write table-driven Go tests that call your Connect handlers against a real Postgres with no Docker, and unit-test business logic with Forge's generated mocks.
- [Find API endpoints that never check who is calling](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/find-endpoints-missing-auth-checks.md): List every signed-in RPC whose handler never reads the caller, then fix each with a role or owner check, or mark it global with a reason a reviewer reads.
- [Scan Go, npm and container dependencies for vulnerabilities](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/scan-dependencies-vulnerabilities.md): Fail CI on vulnerable Go and npm dependencies with govulncheck and npm audit, accept one advisory at a time with a reason and expiry date, and scan the image.
- [Connect Claude Code or Cursor to Forge over MCP](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/connect-claude-code-cursor-mcp.md): Give Claude Code or Cursor Forge's lint, generate, skills and shapes as MCP tools, check the server answers, and add the hosted connector for telemetry.
- [Keep your test suite fast: mark slow tests and enforce budgets](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/keep-test-suite-fast.md): Find the Go tests that slow every edit, mark them with testkit.Slow so they leave the -short tier, and fail CI when a new slow test arrives unmarked.
- [Debug a running Go service from the terminal or an agent](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/debug-go-service-delve-cli.md): Stop a Forge Go service on a breakpoint inside a handler, send it a request, and read its arguments and locals with forge debug, one command per step.
- [Upgrade Forge and apply its migration playbooks](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/forge/upgrade-forge-version.md): Move a project's pinned Forge version forward: preview the change with --check, list the migration playbooks, run project upgrade, and review the diff.
- [How Reliant hosting works: what runs where](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/inside-reliant-hosting.md): Where each part of a hosted forge app runs: the CDN edge and static origin, the environment namespace with default-deny networking, managed Postgres, and the limits.
- [Deploy a Go API with managed Postgres to Reliant hosting](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/deploy-go-api-managed-postgres.md): Ship a Forge Go API, its migrations and a managed Postgres to production as one release, then prove it healthy with forge obs check.
- [Create a preview environment for every pull request](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/preview-environment-every-pull-request.md): Give each pull request its own hosted copy of your app on its own URL, created and deleted from GitHub Actions, and cleaned up by itself when it expires.
- [Add a custom domain with automatic HTTPS](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/custom-domain-https.md): Serve a hosted environment on a hostname you own: claim it, publish the CNAME and TXT records forge prints, bind a workload, and get HTTPS issued for you.
- [Manage production secrets per environment](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/manage-production-secrets.md): Give each environment its own secret values: a gitignored file for dev, the write-only hosted store for prod, set from stdin and rotated without a redeploy.
- [Deploy a Forge app to your own Kubernetes cluster](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/deploy-to-your-own-kubernetes.md): Bind a Forge environment to a Kubernetes cluster you run, deploy a release to it with forge env deploy, and optionally hand delivery to an in-cluster Flux.
- [Keep Helm, Fly.io or Cloud Run and still get releases and gates](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/keep-helm-fly-cloud-run.md): Bind a workload to forge.OnExternal so forge builds, releases and checks it while your own Helm chart, Fly.io app or Cloud Run service keeps deploying it.
- [Call a hosted Forge API from a frontend on Vercel, Netlify or your own host](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/call-hosted-api-from-frontend-elsewhere.md): Keep your frontend where it is and call a Forge API on Reliant hosting, with sign-in that works: a same-site API hostname, credentialed CORS, and the frontend declared as the sign-in origin.
- [Stop a hosted environment when you're not using it](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/stop-hosted-environment.md): Suspend a hosted environment's workloads and database with forge env stop, keep its release and data, and bring it back with forge env start.
- [Promote a release from staging to production by digest](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/promote-release-staging-to-production.md): Move the exact release staging runs to production without a rebuild, approve the plan you read by its digest, and see a stale promotion refused.
- [Gate a production deploy on release health](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/gate-production-deploy-release-health.md): Hold production until staging proves a release healthy: declare a health gate in prod's KCL, judge staging with forge obs check, then promote the release.
- [Recover from a bad deploy by redeploying an earlier release](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/recover-from-bad-deploy.md): Put production back on the last good release in one deploy, check that rollback floors allow it, and set a floor so nobody deploys behind a release again.
- [Deploy from GitHub Actions with an API token](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/deploy-from-github-actions.md): Ship every push to main from GitHub Actions: store a scoped deploy token, cut the release and print its plan in one job, then approve that exact plan in the next.
- [Detect drift between declared and live environments](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/detect-config-drift.md): Check that an environment runs the release it should, and find what your checkout declares but never deployed, with env status, env diff and env verify.
- [Restore a managed Postgres database to a point in time](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/restore-postgres-point-in-time.md): Undo a bad delete on Reliant hosting: declare a new managed Postgres restored from backups to the moment before it, check the rows, and point your app at it.
- [Invite and manage your app's users from the CLI](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/hosting/manage-app-users-cli.md): Invite people to your hosted app, change their roles, lock them out and end their sessions from the terminal, with forge cloud identity on Reliant hosting.
- [How Reliant judges a release: from a span to a verdict](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/deep-dives/how-release-verdicts-work.md): How Reliant turns spans, issues and alerts into a PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE verdict per release, and why missing telemetry is never read as a pass.
- [Send OpenTelemetry from any app to Reliant](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/send-opentelemetry-from-any-app.md): Send traces, logs and metrics from an app in any language to Reliant's hosted OpenTelemetry backend: mint a token with forge obs init and set the variables.
- [Find your slowest API endpoints with per-RPC p95 latency](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/find-slowest-rpcs.md): Rank every RPC by p95 latency with forge obs endpoints, open its slowest traces, and see the N+1 query or CPU work behind it, locally or in production.
- [Route production alerts to Slack, PagerDuty or email](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/route-alerts-slack-pagerduty.md): Send Forge's default alerts to Slack, PagerDuty or email: create receivers in your organization, then route by severity with forge.AlertRoute in KCL.
- [Write alert rules as code and test them locally](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/custom-alert-rules-as-code.md): Declare an alert rule in KCL as a SQL query, check it against your local stack's telemetry, watch it fire on your machine, and ship it with the next release.
- [Build a dashboard in the UI and keep it as code](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/dashboard-ui-to-code.md): Build a dashboard panel by panel in the console or from the terminal, commit it as a file that ships with every release, and check that each panel has data.
- [Add a custom metric without a cardinality explosion](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/add-custom-metric.md): Declare a business metric with a unit and a closed set of attribute keys, record it from a handler, and query it with forge obs without one series per user.
- [Count active, new and returning users from product events](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/active-users-from-product-events.md): Record what signed-in users do with observe.Track, deploy, and read active, new and returning users per environment with forge obs users, no analytics SDK.
- [Find which release introduced a production error](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/find-release-that-caused-error.md): Trace a production error to the release and commits that introduced it with forge obs issue, then resolve it in the next release so a recurrence reopens it.
- [Debug production with an AI agent: logs, traces and errors](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/debug-production-with-ai-agent.md): Let an AI agent find why production fails: read errors, logs and traces with forge obs, follow one request to the failing line, and verify the fix.
- [Debug frontend errors with session timelines and replay](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/debug-frontend-errors-session-timelines.md): Go from a browser error to its source-mapped stack and the session it happened in, then choose per environment whether Forge records a masked replay.
- [Find CPU hotspots with continuous profiling](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/find-cpu-hotspots-continuous-profiling.md): Find the Go function burning your CPU: turn on continuous profiling, read the flamegraph, export pprof with forge obs profile, and narrow it to one trace.
- [Read browser and backend logs in one place during development](https://docs.reliantlabs.io/guides/observability/browser-and-backend-logs-locally.md): Find a browser error, its stack and the backend request it failed on with one grep over .forge/logs/dev, then query the same errors with forge obs locally.
